name: rMG – Image Optimizer
author: Preston Elrod / ProxSEO

sections.description:
rMG – Image Optimizer improves image delivery by analyzing how images are actually displayed on your published WordPress pages.

Instead of only compressing uploads or relying on existing WordPress thumbnail sizes, rMG can inspect selected public pages at configured desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports. It measures displayed image dimensions and creates separate optimized variants for those placements.

Your original Media Library uploads remain unchanged.

Optimize the rendered page

rMG focuses on how images are used after the page layout has rendered. This helps reduce the delivery of images that are much larger than the space where they appear.

Key features include:

  • Post-render analysis of selected published pages.
  • Right-sized variants for desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
  • WebP and AVIF output formats.
  • Page-specific image optimization and reoptimization.
  • Adjustable quality, sharpening, lazy loading, and fade-in controls.
  • Page-level image savings and optimization status.
  • Management and removal of generated variants.
  • Original Media Library uploads remain untouched.

If an optimized variant is unavailable, the original image remains available as a fallback.

rMG is a free service provided by ProxSEO.

External Services

This plugin connects to the hosted ProxSEO rMG image optimization service when an administrator starts site optimization, requests optimization for a page, or runs queued background optimization.

The service analyzes selected published pages, measures displayed image dimensions, and returns analysis results to the WordPress site. The plugin creates optimized image variants locally on the WordPress server.

The service may receive:

  • The site URL and site name.
  • The installed plugin version.
  • The installed WordPress version.
  • Selected published page URLs or page IDs.
  • Configured viewport names.
  • Image and page metadata required for optimization.

The service may request selected publicly accessible pages to analyze how their images are displayed to visitors.

Service provider: ProxSEO / rMG

Terms of Service: https://proxseo.com/rmg-image-optimizer/terms-of-service/

Privacy Policy: https://proxseo.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Install rMG – Image Optimizer through the WordPress plugin directory, or upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/rmg-image-optimizer.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open the rMG admin menu.
  4. Review the image format, quality, viewport, and delivery settings.
  5. Start site-wide optimization or optimize selected published pages.
sections.faq:
What makes rMG different from other image optimizers?

Many image optimizers compress uploaded files or use existing WordPress image sizes. rMG analyzes selected rendered pages, measures how images are displayed at configured viewports, and creates variants for those placements.

Will rMG change my original images?

No. Your original Media Library uploads remain unchanged. rMG creates separate optimized variants that can be removed without deleting the source files.

Which image formats does rMG support?

rMG can generate optimized images in WebP or AVIF format.

How does rMG optimize images for different devices?

rMG analyzes configured desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports separately, then creates variants based on how images are displayed within those layouts.

Can I optimize individual pages?

Yes. You can optimize or reoptimize selected published pages, run site-wide optimization, or leave specific pages untouched.

Does rMG use an external service?

Yes. Page analysis uses the hosted ProxSEO rMG service. Image variants are generated locally by the plugin. See the External Services section for details about when the service is contacted and what information may be sent.
sections.changelog:
0.3.2

  • Added site-wide phase progress that aggregates all bounded mini-batches.
  • Added completed phase indicators for queueing, crawling, and image generation.
  • Prioritized the next page group so faster-image generation can continue in the background during page checks.
  • Added friendlier progress wording and an animated active progress indicator.
  • Added an outlined Save and regenerate action beside the normal settings save button.

0.3.1

  • Fixed bugs with high-page website optimization.
  • Improved Error Handling

0.3.0

  • Initial public release of rMG – Image Optimizer.
